paper.title: Shaping contactless radiation forces through anomalous acoustic scattering

parameter_policy: Original source paraphrases and locators only; no powered settings, exposure recipe, physical acceptance constants or source-derived success thresholds.

facts.claim: Three fabricated groove-pattern designs are studied on a suspended torsion pendulum; there is no free-flight levitation demonstration.
Metasurface 1 targets lateral actuation, Metasurface 2 targets one-axis self-guiding, and Metasurface 3 targets attractive actuation.

Photopolymer jetting is the stated fabrication method. Sideways print orientation is reported to reduce overflow into grooves. Resin identity, postprocessing and acceptance tolerances are not supplied.
Metasurface 1 has 30 cells and a separately reported outer envelope. Metasurface 2 has 30 cells; Metasurface 3 deliberately has 20. Do not assign the first envelope to every design.
facts.locator: MAIN p2 and p6; SI p5
facts.numeric_values_policy: Historical values remain in the separately reviewed source packet; not actor inputs or operating defaults.

facts.claim: The pendulum uses a tungsten fiber, aluminum rod, counterweight, central mirror and screen camera. The reported sensitivity is not an independently verified calibration.

facts.claim: A camera tracks a reflected laser spot and baseline-subtracted displacement is plotted. The full pixel-to-screen-to-angle-to-specimen transform and uncertainty are not specified.
Reported acoustic actuation uses piezoelectric transducers and design-dependent source arrays. Nonuniform output and temporal changes motivated down-selection.

facts.claim: Metasurface 1 has an on/off displacement trace and equilibrium-displacement versus source-voltage comparison. Recovery toward the initial equilibrium is shown after source off.
A flipped metasurface is reported to reverse the deflection sign. A separate flat unpatterned specimen test is not reported.
Metasurface 2 follows a changing source on one axis. The experimental plot has source angle in degrees and displacement in centimetres, on separate axes.
For the centered mirror-symmetric self-guiding design the source describes zero lateral force, not zero total acoustic force.
Metasurface 3 displacement changes from attractive to repulsive at an approximately reported attack angle. This is a reported result, not a future success threshold.

facts.claim: Main experimental error bars are identified as standard deviation, but Methods also calls them a confidence interval. Replicate count and independent experimental units are not stated.
facts.locator: MAIN p3 Fig 2f; p5 Fig 4d; p6 Methods

facts.claim: The source models acoustic radiation force through stress-tensor integration and compares it with an analytical prism model. These are numerical/theoretical comparisons, not physical reference-force calibration.
facts.locator: MAIN p6; SI p4 Fig S3

facts.claim: Main field maps and force curves from finite elements are not measured wave fields. Simulated force per length and normalized force are not experimental force in newtons. The paper compares a two-dimensional static-object model with an experiment in which the specimen moves; predicted trends are not a matched geometry or magnitude validation.
Numerical configurations differ: M1 and M3 use the stated experimental separation, whereas the M2 field illustration uses a larger separation.

facts.claim: The first groove design is refined by numerical optimization from an analytical design; the second is assembled from mirror-symmetric analytical steering structures without numerical optimization; the third is numerically optimized for pulling.
The source-reported optimization improvements are numerical comparisons; no paired physical test of all corresponding baseline designs is established.

facts.claim: Movie 1 shows a different orientation with the patterned face visible from above. Movie 2 uses a downward-facing patterned surface with the source below; Movie 3 uses the latter family with a curved source holder.
SI geometric reasoning isolates torsion about vertical z from the desired horizontal force; it does not empirically exclude every parasitic force or qualify safety.
Biology, medicine and robotic surgery occur as cited or prospective applications. The actual reported specimens in this paper are inert fabricated structures.
